clue.text: Insect-bitten lion unable to stand up on its own

definitions.text: unable to stand up on its own

indicators.note: a creature that is bitten has something in its flesh, so the insect sits inside the lion

parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A lion has been bitten by insects and can no longer get to its feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insect-bitten' splits so 'bitten' is the container signal. A lean-to is a shed built against a wall, which it needs for support.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed propped against a wall, relying on it for support.

clue.text: Get at a sealed container on the outside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter a is shut inside the container as if sealed in it
the container wraps round the letter a, staying on its outside

parts.note: a tin is a metal container

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get at the contents of a sealed container from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sealed' and 'on the outside' both say the container closes round the A; 'Get at' looks like one phrase but 'Get' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain something is to reach or achieve it, a synonym of get.

clue.text: It offers superior facilities for training

definitions.text: It offers superior facilities for training

parts.words: It offers superior facilities for training
parts.note: superior means up above, and training means travelling by train: an elevated line carrying trains over the streets

explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' looks like 'excellent' and 'training' like coaching, but they mean physically above and going by train.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevated railway runs trains above street level, so its transport is raised up.

clue.text: She is taken over a bumpy road, apparently

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is taken over something is placed above, so it comes first

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a bumpy road is uneven, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A woman is driven along an uneven road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken over' places the first parts above the rest in this down entry; 'apparently' is a link. Isadora Duncan was a famous dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Isadora is a woman's first name, as in the dancer Isadora Duncan.

clue.text: Busy sight that meets the eves when looking at a navigable river?

definitions.text: Busy sight that meets the eves when looking at a navigable river?

parts.words: Busy sight that meets the eves when looking at a navigable river?
parts.note: a navigable river carries a constant flow of boats, a busy watercourse full of vessels; eves is printed for eyes

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally describes cars on a road; here it is taken literally as boats on a river. 'eves' is almost certainly a misprint for 'eyes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A continuous flow of vehicles is a phrase for congestion; on a waterway it is the boats passing.

clue.text: Daring display of non-cooperation

explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is both bold challenge and an open refusal to comply with authority.

clue.text: Avid for food, I use rent indiscriminately

indicators.note: done without care or order, so the letters are mixed at random

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A hungry tenant spends the rent money on whatever comes along.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a formal word meaning hungry or greedy.

clue.text: Once vast collection foreign coins

indicators.note: a collection gathers the letters together into a new arrangement

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A coin collection that was once enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Centavos are small coins of several Latin American countries and Portugal's old currency.

clue.text: A god-fearing man, he is outstandingly sober

indicators.note: standing outside, so the word for sober wraps around the other letters

parts.note: TT means teetotal, never drinking
taken as written

explanation.surface: A religious man who is remarkably abstemious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstandingly' reads as 'remarkably' but splits as standing outside. TT (teetotal) is a crossword staple for sober.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist believes in a god, so a pious believer fits.

clue.text: Look warm and dry

definitions.meaning: to put laundry somewhere warm to finish drying

explanation.definitionFit: An air is a manner or appearance; to air clothes is to warm them until fully dry.

clue.text: Single Engineers brought in without remuneration

indicators.note: the engineers are put inside the other word

parts.note: unpaid means receiving no pay
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A lone group of engineers is brought on to work for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' is the container signal. RE (Royal Engineers) is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpaired means not matched with a partner, so on its own.

clue.text: Frenchman who couldn't adapt to new regime?

definitions.text: Frenchman who couldn't adapt to new regime?

indicators.note: a new form of the word, its letters rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who fled because he could not accept the post-revolutionary government.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, 'new regime' is an anagram; as a whole, the clue describes an aristocrat who left France after the Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is an exile, especially a royalist who fled the French Revolution.

clue.text: It could take the form of a sharp dig in the ribs, presumably

definitions.text: It could take the form of a sharp dig in the ribs, presumably

parts.words: It could take the form of a sharp dig in the ribs, presumably
parts.note: a sharp elbow nudge to make someone remember, read literally as a jab with a point

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for an unsubtle hint is taken literally: a prod that is physically sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed reminder is a pointed hint, here pictured as a jab in the side.

clue.text: One writing up a particular doctrine or theory

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Someone writes up an account of a doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses only the writing in this down entry; MS (manuscript) is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is any distinctive doctrine or system of belief.

clue.text: Unbendingly they press home the charge

definitions.text: Unbendingly they press home the charge

parts.words: Unbendingly they press home the charge
parts.note: stiff rods used to push the powder and ball down a muzzle-loading gun, though the surface suggests determined attackers

explanation.walkthrough: 'press home the charge' sounds like pushing an attack or an accusation; it is loading a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramrod is a rigid rod for tamping the charge into a muzzle-loader's barrel.

clue.text: A skinflint holding to a spray-gun, possibly

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a miser is a skinflint, someone mean with money
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mean person keeps hold of a spray-gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal; 'possibly' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser turns liquid into a fine spray, like a small spray-gun.

clue.text: Suites made out of 7

indicators.note: the answer is formed from the letters of the other entry, rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 7 down, a word meaning hungry

explanation.definitionFit: A suite can be a train of attendants, the same as a retinue.

clue.text: Brings about results

explanation.definitionFit: To effect is to cause something; effects are its consequences.

clue.text: A green isle in the Aegean

definitions.meaning: a long-leaved lettuce, a salad vegetable
a Greek island in the Dodecanese, also spelt Kos

explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a type of lettuce, a green, and also a Greek island near Turkey.

clue.text: A motor-cycle race round trees to begin with

indicators.note: the race goes around the trees

parts.note: TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race
firs are trees

explanation.surface: A motorbike race circles some trees at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal. The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: At first means initially, at the beginning.

clue.text: Top painters?

parts.note: painters of the top of a person, their head and face, not leading painters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like 'best', but it means the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Portraitists paint faces and heads, the top of a person.

clue.text: Really put in the form of a question?

definitions.text: put in the form of a question?
definitions.meaning: said with a questioning lift, it is a reply of surprise meaning is that so

explanation.definitionFit: Indeed means truly; as a one-word question it expresses doubt or surprise.

clue.text: The code of Old Jewry

parts.note: the body of Jewish civil and religious law; Old Jewry is also a London street

explanation.walkthrough: Old Jewry is a street in the City of London, so the clue looks like a reference to a postal code or local rule.
explanation.definitionFit: The Talmud is the ancient compendium of rabbinic law and teaching.

clue.text: Remarkable way to pass on information

explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means striking; as a noun it is a sign that conveys a message.

clue.text: They do not believe in going to fresh fields

indicators.note: the second part goes next to the first, following it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Sceptics have no faith in moving on to fresh fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of 'believe in', but it supplies letters; 'fresh' is the anagram signal and 'going to' joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Infidels are unbelievers, those without the faith.

clue.text: A series of big fights, maybe

definitions.text: A series of big fights, maybe

parts.words: A series of big fights, maybe
parts.note: a succession of battles, rather than a boxing programme

explanation.walkthrough: 'big fights' suggests boxing, but means battles.
explanation.definitionFit: A war is a conflict made up of many battles.

clue.text: Group of gymnasts given a trifling amount of overseas currency

parts.note: PE is physical education, gymnastics at school
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A gym team is handed a few coins of foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: The order is PE then SET then A.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was Spain's unit of currency, worth little.

clue.text: Files put out with malicious intent

indicators.note: put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone throws out the files out of spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiteful means wishing harm, mean-spirited.
